notes.purpose: jaxfne/optim implements the optimizer layer sitting behind Model.tune() — optimizer "spec" construction (GSDR/AGSDR/random_search/optax_adam/optax_sgd/GSGD), the blackbox candidate-proposal loop actually driving tuning, several Optax-integrated "*_transform" gradient-transformation factories, plus small shared utilities (parameter bounds/clipping, manifest serialization). Internally it is a core+satellites split: one dominant file (core.py, 1893 lines, 83% of the subpackage's line count) holds essentially everything with real behavior — OptimizerSpec/AGSDROptimizerSpec dataclasses (core.py:97,178), the spec builders `gsdr`/`agsdr`/`random_search`/`optax_adam`/`optax_sgd`/`gsgd` (lines 158,243,325,336,359,379), the dispatcher `_resolve_optimizer` (line 403), the actual blackbox loop `propose_blackbox_candidates`/`_run_agsdr_optimization_loop` (lines 509,573), and three Optax-integrated `*_transform` factories (`sdr_transform`/`gsdr_transform`/`agsdr_transform`, lines 866/1002/1123) plus three private `_tune_*_optax` differentiable-path helpers (lines 1282,1652,1767) — while five small standalone files (`base.py`, `bounds.py`, `sdr.py`, `gsdr.py`, `agsdr.py`, `gsgd.py`, `manifests.py`, each 16-58 lines) each own one narrow concern: shared dataclass state, bounds clipping, and per-optimizer-family low-level `step_*_transform` plain-SGD steps that are explicitly documented as NOT the real behavior their names imply.
key_findings: 9 files (excluding __pycache__/.DS_Store): __init__.py(86), agsdr.py(58), base.py(16), bounds.py(29), core.py(1893), gsdr.py(55), gsgd.py(41), manifests.py(49), sdr.py(50) — total 2277 lines (`wc -l jaxfne/optim/*.py`).
core.py alone is 75888 bytes / 1893 lines vs. all other files combined at ~384 lines — a stark core+satellites split, not one-file-per-concern uniformly.

__init__.py (jaxfne/optim/__init__.py:50-78) __all__ lists 26 public names (step_*_transform x4, apply/enforce_parameter_bounds, serialize_optimization_manifest, *State x4, AGSDR, AGSDROptimizerSpec, OptimizerSpec, agsdr/agsdr_transform/gsdr/gsdr_transform/gsgd/optax_adam/optax_sgd/random_search/require_optax/sdr_transform, propose_blackbox_candidates, quadratic_target_loss_grad).

5 names are imported into __init__.py but deliberately excluded from __all__ (jaxfne/optim/__init__.py:79-86): `_agsdr_candidates_from_noise`, `_run_agsdr_optimization_loop`, `_quadratic_target_loss`, `_resolve_optimizer`, `_tune_matrix_agsdr_optax` (and two more `_tune_source_scale_optax`/`_tune_scalar_soft_rate_optax` imported at lines 46-47 but also absent from __all__) — internal-only but still directly importable, e.g. `_resolve_optimizer` is used by tests/test_v0317_dtype_invariants.py per the __init__.py comment (lines 82-86).

pyproject.toml:105 has an explicit `"jaxfne/optim/__init__.py" = ["F401"]` ruff per-file-ignore, confirming __init__.py is a deliberate re-export aggregator (per FRICTIONS_STACK.md F-030) and its imports must not be auto-fixed away.

sdr.py:24-46, gsdr.py:24-55, agsdr.py:25-58 all document, verbatim in their own docstrings, that `step_{sdr,gsdr,agsdr}_transform` are plain gradient-descent (`u_t - eta*grad_l`) despite their state dataclasses (SDRState/GSDRState with deselection_counter/AGSDRState with deselection_counter+alpha_adaptive) implying more elaborate stochastic-delta/genetic/adaptive behavior — state is passed through unchanged, unused fields never read.

gsgd.py:24-37 documents the same plain-SGD gap for GSGD, and further states the differentiable-optimizer branch of Model.tune() (`optax_guarded_path`) is 'a metadata-only guard that returns without ever entering a gradient loop' — step_gsgd_transform is not invoked by production tuning as of the file's writing.

sdr.py/gsdr.py/agsdr.py each confirm (dated 2026-07-18) that Model.tune(optimizer="SDR"/"GSDR"/"AGSDR") dispatches via `_resolve_optimizer` (core.py:403) to the blackbox `propose_blackbox_candidates`/`_run_agsdr_optimization_loop` path (core.py:509,573), which never calls the corresponding `*_transform` factory in core.py — i.e. two independent, same-named implementations coexist per optimizer family, and neither the low-level step_*_transform files nor the higher-level core.py *_transform factories are the actual call path.

bounds.py:22-29 documents `apply_parameter_constraints` as a pure alias of `enforce_parameter_bounds` — previously two independently-duplicated byte-identical bodies, now merged to delegate (matches git log commit 38ca582-style dedup pattern seen elsewhere in this repo).

core.py's own module docstring (lines 1-15) states the 'optimizer grammar': optimizer_class ∈ {differentiable, blackbox, hybrid, multiparameter_blackbox}; optimizer ∈ {GSDR, AGSDR, random_search, optax_adam, optax_sgd}; differentiability_status and surrogate_status enums — this is the closest thing to a subpackage contract.

Outputs are handled as a structured simulation proxy (amplitude_claim_allowed=False)' (agsdr.py:3-4, gsdr.py:3-4, sdr.py:3-4, gsgd.py:3-4, manifests.py:3-4) — a repo-wide truth-gate marker, not optim-specific prose.
contracts: Optimizer grammar contract stated in core.py:9-14 (docstring): optimizer_class must be one of differentiable|blackbox|hybrid|multiparameter_blackbox; optimizer name must be one of GSDR|AGSDR|random_search|optax_adam|optax_sgd; differentiability_status one of differentiable|declared_surrogate|non_differentiable|not_checked; surrogate_status one of none|declared|required_but_missing|not_applicable — enforced in code via frozensets `_BLACKBOX_OPTIMIZERS`/`_DIFFERENTIABLE_OPTIMIZERS`/`_ALL_KNOWN_OPTIMIZERS`/`_VALID_DIFFERENTIABILITY`/`_VALID_SURROGATE`/`_VALID_OPTIMIZER_CLASS` (core.py:25-35).
